custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin who can switch between two locations: the test location and location B.
  • Create part A for this test at the test location only, and leave it active.
  • Create part B for this test at both locations under the same part number, inactive at the test location and active at location B.
  • Create part C for this test at location B only, and set it inactive there, so location B's Inactive tab has a part it must list.
  • Give parts A, B and C part numbers that start with the same text, so one search lists all three.
  • Start on the test location's Inventory page, on the Active tab.

How to set this up on the QA site (https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com):

  • Admin at the test location: on the QA site's sign-in screen choose Admin. The test location is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; its name shows in the box at the top right. If another name shows, click that box, click the name beside Change Location: and pick Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Location B is Staging Lethbridge - 4310. To switch: click the box at the top right, click the name beside Change Location: and pick Staging Lethbridge - 4310. Switch back to Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 the same way.
  • To create a part: click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill Description and Part Number (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C425585-A for part A, -B for part B), pick a Category, type a Cost and a Sell Price, type the Quantity in the bin row (the location's bin, for example General Storage, is offered), then click Save. Leave Track quantities and cost of goods on for a tracked part; click it off for an untracked part. Add Bin Location adds a second bin; Vendor, Manufacturer, Core Charge, Min, Max and Tags are in the same window. Parts that must start with the same text all start ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C425585-, so searching for that finds them all.
  • The Search box above the Inventory list opens when you click Search (the magnifier).
  • To set a part inactive: on the Inventory page's Active tab click Search, type its part number, click its row; in Edit Inventory Part click Inactive under Part Status, click Save, then click Deactivate in the Deactivate part? window. The part then shows on the Inactive tab.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part A is listed on the Active tab.
  • Parts B and C are not listed.

Step 2:

  • The Inactive tab is selected.

Step 3:

  • Part B is listed on the Inactive tab.
  • Parts A and C are not listed.

Step 4:

  • The location selector shows location B.

Step 5:

  • The Parts left menu shows Inventory.

Step 6:

  • Location B's Inventory page opens on the Active tab.

Step 7:

  • Part B is listed on location B's Active tab, because it is still active there.
  • Part A is not listed, because it is not stocked at location B.

Step 8:

  • The Inactive tab is selected.

Step 9:

  • Part C is listed on location B's Inactive tab.
  • Neither part A nor part B is listed there: making part B inactive at the test location did not change it at location B.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10814 (Story 1, Active and Inactive Tabs on the Inventory List)

  • S1-R3: “The Active tab lists only parts that are active at the current location.”
  • S1-R4: “The Inactive tab lists only parts that are inactive at the current location.”
  • Feature Overview, Core functionality: “Both states belong to the part at one location. The same part at another location keeps its own states.”
  • Key Decisions: “Active and tracked are set per location. A part is stocked at a location, and whether the shop still sells it, or counts it, is that location's call. Changing either state at one location never changes the same part at another location.”

Last checked against build v26.43.4-999c51d (QA site sv10647) on 11/3/2026.
